content.body:
The Char Léger mle 1935 Renault was selected early on as the natural replacement for the obsolescent FT17 still scattered in deployments across France. Never considered to have a particularly impressive main gun, it was heavily armored and its all-cast construction was novel for the time. Pitifully slow (most infantry can outrun it), the tank was really outclassed from the very beginning of the conflict, but could still come out ahead with a skilled crew or overconfident opponents.
The R-35 tends to be the last tank picked from the available list, for good reason: it is slow and poorly armed. But it is not entirely impotent, and its small profile can make it quite effective in certain defensive situations. With an R-35 you really need to forget you can move unless near death, and treat yourself like an armored movable pillbox. Supporting an infantry attack, you can stick it in gear and move while shooting the gun, as you will not outdistance your supporting infantry. Pay particular attention to AT guns, they can penetrate you if you let them get close enough.
Make sure you don't accidentally open the gunner's port. On other tanks, this would leave a very small vulnerability in the mantlet; on French tanks it opens a gaping port on the entire back of the turret leaving your turret members entirely exposed to even pistol fire.
Control Variations: Driver zooms in on view slit with (key O to open). No periscope, closing view slit armor blocks view completely. Commander is in a cupola, cannot unbutton. View is through an armored view slit (key O to open). No view elevation change. View traverse speed limited to turret traverse speed. Gunner has an open view port in front of him, non-closeable, unusable.
